hmed-01-c2.text: National Library of Medicine, History of Medicine Division. Greek Medicine. U.S. National Library of Medicine.
hmed-01-c2.quote: The four bodily fluids, or humors, of blood, phlegm, yellow bile, and black bile
hmed-01-c2.claim: In Hippocratic medicine, your health was a balance between the four humours: blood, phlegm, yellow bile, and black bile.

hmed-02-c2.text: Mark Cartwright (2023). William Harvey's Discovery of Blood Circulation. World History Encyclopedia.
hmed-02-c2.quote: in 1661 when the presence of capillaries between the veins and arteries was discovered by Marcello Malpighi (1628-1694) using a microscope
hmed-02-c2.claim: The capillaries Harvey had hypothesised as connecting arteries to veins were finally directly observed by Marcello Malpighi in 1661, using the newly developed microscope.

hmed-04-c1.text: U.S. National Library of Medicine. Smallpox: Success. U.S. National Library of Medicine.
hmed-04-c1.quote: it was not until 1980 that the WHO felt confident that smallpox had been completely eradicated.
hmed-04-c1.claim: The disease was declared eradicated in 1980: the first and so far only human disease ever wiped out by deliberate effort.
